details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N]. The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires: no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107) * sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing sees the same benefit. Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently producing a degraded backend.
